translationLoss.explanation: I checked the document against the abstract process one rule at a time, and every rule matches. The data matches: volume, upper mark, lower mark, starting mix and the charge table equal C, U, D, the starting levels and the intake table, and the line limit equals G = 38. Intake is uncapped: "Volume is not enforced in this step." Spill-over is sequential and can cascade: "Handle the forms one at a time, in the order 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6." Both trigger boundaries are inclusive: "at least its upper mark" and "at most its lower mark." The hysteresis rule is kept: "keeps whatever status it had." Release amounts are computed first and applied together: "Work out all six amounts before changing any form. Then apply all six together." Bleed goes to n-1, and form 1's goes to waste. Excess after settle is not capped and persists in cycle 5: "it is never dealt with and stays in the form." The reset threshold is strict: "more than 38" fires and "38 or less" does not. Rounding is defined with examples. The only unstated point is that Step 4 uses the status set in Step 3. The document's phrase "a GREEN form's settle amount" means the form's current status, and that is the abstract reading too, so I count no rule as lost, blurred or added.

domainPull: The pull was strongest in Step 4. There, mix \"bleeds back up the chute\" to the form before it, while real material only flows downhill. The same step lets a form \"hold more than its volume\", and in cycle 5 that excess stays, which real forms cannot do. A second pull is the reversible GREEN/HOT status, since real curing only goes one way. No operator fell for any of these. All three noted that forms 2 and 4 end above their volumes after cycle 5.
